subject: general
question: A shopkeeper allows 18% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 23%. If he gains ₹1,840 on the sale of the article, then what is the marked price of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Profit × (100 + Profit%) ÷ Profit%

⇒ SP = 1840 × (123 ÷ 23) = ₹9,840

Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)

⇒ MP = 9840 × (100 ÷ 82) = ₹12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 18%

Profit = 23%

Gain (Profit amount) = ₹1,840

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

SP = CP + Profit

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d81980c180b70d32529c2a71946b8892da5e6d7a14a2a300c55c167a1c40386a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 23% of CP = 1840

⇒ CP = (1840 × 100) ÷ 23 = ₹8,000

⇒ SP = CP + Profit = 8000 + 1840 = ₹9,840

⇒ We know that SP = MP × (100 − 18) ÷ 100

⇒ 9840 = MP × (82 ÷ 100)

⇒ 9840 = 0.82 × MP

⇒ MP = 9840 ÷ 0.82

⇒ MP = ₹12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price can be directly found using: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, the Profit% = (Error ÷ True Value − Error) × 100.
